diagnoses.name: Anaemia
diagnoses.text1:
1. Limit blood loss and supportive care

- Stop any active bleeding
- Keep warm
- Support feeding
diagnoses.text2:
2. Send FBC, Group and cross match

- Evaluate causes
diagnoses.text3:
3. Consider blood transfusion if...

- Severe anaemia - paper white appearance
- Associated respiratory distress
- Signs of heart failure
- if infant symptomatic or underlying condition likely to benefit from increased Hb give transfusion

For acute blood loss: replace estimate loss

For more chronic anaemia (from multiple samples or anaemia of prematurity) use the formula: amount required (mls packed cells)= weight (kg) x desired increase in Hb x 3. 

10-15 ml/kg of packed cells is unlikely to go wrong. 

Rate: 5-10ml/kg/hour.

1ml/kg frusemide should be given one hour after the start or halfway through.
If >15ml/kg calculated volume, consider splitting over consecutive days especially if there is a PDA

Prescribe iron but not if the baby has high fever & sepsis - wait for acute infection to settle

diagnoses.name: Convulsions
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Convulsions seen on examination or history
diagnoses.text1:
1. Airway management & oxygen
- Neutral position
- Check for secretions, suction if needed 
- Put on oxygen
diagnoses.text2:
2. Check blood glucose
- If < 47 mg/dl or < 2.6 mmol/L give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- If blood glucose monitoring not available give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
- Do full infection screen (blood culture, lumbar puncture, CRP if age is more than 36 hours)
- Take blood for Ca, Mg, U and E’s, FBC
diagnoses.text3:
3. Give anticonvulsants
- Give phenobarbitone 20mg/kg IM 
- Repeat loading dose ONCE if necessary
- If seizures ongoing give Phenytoin with a loading dose 20mg/kg  IV 
- If seizures still ongoing - give maintenance phenobarbitone 5mg/kg PO/IM

When seizures have stopped and baby stable click the blue arrow to continue

diagnoses.name: Abandoned baby
diagnoses.text1: Contact Social Work at SMCH for Further assistance.

diagnoses.name: Feeding difficulty
diagnoses.text1:
Below is a simple guide to feeding but please consult Iliff guidelines and wall charts for more detailed management 

1. Baby stable breathing <60bpm

If baby cannot feed adequately by breast or bottle but is stable, try using a cup or spoon 

Feed volumes day by day per kg are seen here.
diagnoses.text2:
2. Tachypnoea, breathing > 60bpm

If baby is breathing fast, tired or struggling to feed, insert a naso/orogastric tube and give feeds down the tube via syringe every 2 hours
diagnoses.text3:
3. Tachypnoea, breathing > 80bpm 

If baby is in significant distress, breathing over 80 times/minute or exhibiting other danger signs, stop feeds and begin IV fluids.

diagnoses.expression: $HPCS = 'PF' or $HPCS = 'Apn' or $HPCS = 'Ltemp' or $PregConditions = ‘DM’ or $ANSteroids = ‘Y’ or $MuscSkel = 'Lethargy' or $Cynosis = 'Y'
diagnoses.expressionMeaning:
Birth weight less than 2500g or greater than 4000g
Gestation less than 37wks
Mother has diabetes or received steroids
Baby admitted for Neonatal Encephalopathy
diagnoses.text1:
A baby presenting with any of the following conditions listed below is at risk of hypoglycaemia:
-	Birth weight <2500g
-	Birth weight >4000g
-	Infants of diabetic mothers
-	Preterm <37 weeks 
-	Maternal beta blocker use
-	Perinatal asphyxia, HIE, Neonatal encephalopathy
-	Late preterm exposure to antenatal steroids
diagnoses.text2:
Monitor blood sugars:
-	Ensure that baby is offered the breast within the first 60 minutes
-	Check blood glucose before the second feed (2-4 hours after birth)
-	If 3 normal blood sugars (>2.6 – 8.3mmol) on postnatal ward or NNU monitoring can be stopped
-	If blood sugar <2.6mmol (or < 47mgdL) follow the hypoglycaemia management pathway

diagnoses.name: Low Birth Weight (1500-2499g)
diagnoses.text1:
Manage this baby according to the weight as below:

Above 1800g:
- May require cup feeds
- Skin-skin & kangaroo care for thermoregulation
- If the baby is feeding well with assistance, warm and not exhibiting any danger signs, the baby can stay with their mother
- If the baby is not feeding well by breast, bottle, or cup or exhibiting any danger signs the baby should stay in neonatal unit
diagnoses.text2:
Less than 1799g:
- Needs admission to neonatal unit for close observation 
- 1500-1799g if not feeding well by breast start cup feeds (change from 2000)
- Those <1500g should be fed by NGT and feeds advanced slowly as per the table

diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby's temperature is recorded as 36 degrees up to 36.4 degrees

Skin to skin (KMC position) or place on warmer or resuscitaire
diagnoses.text2:

- Make sure baby is dry 
- Put on a hat & wrap up the baby  
- If on the resuscitaire put the sides up

diagnoses.text3:

- Complete the Neotree assessment to assess for signs of infection, apnoea and hypoglycaemia

diagnoses.name: Normal Baby
diagnoses.text1:
Routine Care

1. Check if breast feeding well
2. Check if mother has been tested for HIV and refer for testing if HIV status unknown
3. Remind mothers to take infants to the local clinic for review at 3 days
4. Ensure baby has passed urine and stool in first 24 hours. 

If baby less than 24 hours old and has not passed urine or stool, ensure mother knows to seek a review locally or at HCH if stool/urine passage delayed beyond 24 hours.
diagnoses.text2:
Remember to check clinically for:

JAUNDICE 
Cataracts (red reflex)
Talipes: refer to orthopods/physio
Hip dysplasia
Extra digits
Heart murmurs
Anal atresia
diagnoses.text3:
Avoid unnecessary admission

Do not separate the mother from the infant if not absolutely necessary. Consider if observation may be sufficient without admission.

diagnoses.name: Premature (32 to 37 weeks)
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Baby's gestation is 32 weeks to 37 weeks
diagnoses.text1:
Most stable larger preterm babies (>1500g) not needing oxygen may safely be nursed with their mother in Kangaroo Care. 
Remember to perform Ballard Score- images are for neuromuscular followed by physical maturity assessment  - (Ballad score images in script)
diagnoses.text2:
WARM CHAIN is maintained: 
•	Keep the radiant warmer or resucitaire on
•	For babies < 32 weeks deliver into plastic bag before drying if available. If not, dry infant in warm 
towel and wrap in another dry warm towel.
•	Put skin to skin with mother and cover both with blanket
•	Keep room/transport incubator/ambulance (if transporting) as warm as possible.
•	Ensure baby has a hat & socks, and perform procedures in the incubator.

1. Thermoregulation
Keep the baby warm aiming between 36.5-37.5’C by Skin to skin (KMC position) or place on radiant warmer or incubator if available

Mild hypothermia: 36-36.4 --> cause for concern,  warm the baby

Moderate hypothermia: 32-35.9--> DANGER
•	rewarm baby,  
•	check blood glucose

Severe hypothermia <32, outcome likely to be poor, 
•	rewarm baby, 
•	check blood glucose

2. Respiratory support
•	Oxygen / CPAP
•	CPAP >28 weeks or > 1000g and passes the TRY CPAP algorithm (image in script)
•	Remember preterms may have slightly reduced tone due to their prematurity
•	Early CPAP for babies between 28 - 32 weeks
•	Prevention of apnoea Give Caffeine Citrate 20mg/kg orally or slowly by intravenous route over 30 minutes and a maintenance dose of 5mg/kg/day to all preterm babies<32 weeks. Give until 34 weeks postnestrual age.
•	If Caffeine citrate is not available give a loading dose of aminophylline at 6mg/kg over 20 minutes followed by a maintenance dose of 2.5mg/kg every 12 hours
diagnoses.text3:
3. Feeding support 
•	If able to suck GIVE breast feed
•	If not able to suck give cup feeds or consider OGT 
•	OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
•	OGT if on CPAP
•	Consider IV fluids in smaller babies breathing > 80 bpm

diagnoses.name: Respiratory Distress
diagnoses.expression: $HPCS = 'Cough' or $HPCS = 'FB' or $HPCS = 'Wh' or $HPCS = 'Apn' or $HPCS = 'RN' or $HPCS = 'PF' or $PaedsRR > 60 or $Cursats < 90 or $SignsRD = 'CHI' or $SignsRD = 'HN' or $SignsRD = 'Gasp' or $SignsRD = 'GR' or $SignsRD = 'TT' or $SignsRD = 'ST' or $AirEntry = 'PoorAE' or $BreathSounds = 'Bronchial' or $AdBrSounds = 'CrackCrep' or $AdBrSounds = 'Wh' or $RespCVSyst = 'Cough' or $RespCVSyst = 'FB' or $RespCVSyst = 'GR' or $RespCVSyst = 'NBr' or $RespCVSyst = 'Wh'
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Respiratory distress in the neonate and the baby <60 days
diagnoses.text1:
Keep the baby warm, aim for 36.5-37.5°C

Supportive treatment

Give oxygen if O2 Saturation <90% -  baby may need CPAP if low saturations inspite of nasal prongs oxygen

Fluid bolus if signs of shock (10ml/kg 0.9% Sodium Chloride)
Check for signs of congenital heart disease: hepatomegaly, gallop rhythm, weak femoral pulses. 
If concerns give fluid bolus slowly 

Assess for dehydration: 
Give feeds through an OGT (150ml/kg/24 hours) - If not tolerating OGT give fluids IV (100ml/kg/24 hours)

If blood sugar is < 2.6mmol/L give 10% Dextrose 2ml/kg. Check again 1 hour after starting fluids. 

CHECK HIV status if not known or maternal HIV test was not done or done early in pregnancy and baby comes with either severe infection or recurrent infections
diagnoses.text2: Antibiotic guidance
diagnoses.text3:
Blood cultures - REMEMBER to put the Neotree number on the blood culture bottle, minimise contamination by cleaning well with disinfectant and leave the area to dry, put AT LEAST 1-2 ml in the blood culture bottle	

DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS FOR RESPIRATORY DISTRESS
•	Neonatal sepsis 
•	Bacterial Pneumonia: generally unwell looking, high or low temperature, grunting and head bobbing, very difficult to separate from sepsis treat as sepsis if in doubt
•	Lipoid pneumonia: ask about feeding with cooking or anointing oil
•	Viral Bronchiolitis: baby have nasal congestion and/or discharge for a few days before presentation, respiratory distress gets worse on day 6-8, increased work of breathing, tachypnoea, desaturation with crying, coughing, and sleep. 
•	Pertussis (consider if apnoea and do a FBC) 
•	Chronic lung disease ( if baby was born premature and required oxygen >4 weeks) 
•	Congenital heart disease (look for signs of cardiac failure: large liver, gallop rhythm. Loud second heart sound, weak femoral pulses. May be history of poor feeding and poor weight gain. Do CRX and ECHO if able and contact senior urgently for advice.

diagnoses.name: Sepsis suspected
diagnoses.expression: ($Temperature < 36 or $Temperature > 38 ) AND ($HPCS = 'FB' or $HPCS = 'PF' or $HPCS = 'Disa' or $HPCS = 'Sleepy' or $HPCS = 'Irr' or $HPCS = 'Pl' or $HPCS = 'Jaun' or $HPCS = 'Rsh' or $Colour = 'Blue' or $Colour = 'Yell' or $Colour = 'Pale' or $Jaundice = 'Y' or $Umbilicus = 'Inf') AND ($CRT = 'Prol' or $Warm = 'Cold')
diagnoses.text1: Consider neonatal severe infections if any Major Criteria or two or more Minor Criteria are met:
diagnoses.text2: Antibiotic Treatment:
diagnoses.text3:
MANAGEMENT
Keep baby warm and aim for temperature between 36.5-37.5 
Stabilise the infant using the ABCD resuscitation principles 

TAKE:
1)	Blood culture 
(REMEMBER to put the Neotree number on the blood culture bottle, minimise contamination by cleaning well with disinfectant and leave the area to dry, put AT LEAST 1-2 ml in the blood culture bottle) DON’T delay giving antibiotics if blood culture not possible 
2)	Perform a Lumbar puncture in ALL babies under 2 months of age 
3)	Urine Dipstick and culture for LOS: urine culture need to be sterile, need to clean the perineum. Don’t delay antibiotics to wait for urine culture – do not send if you cannot catch a sterile sample
GIVE: 
1)	Antibiotics (see below)
2)	Oxygen if sats <90% in air
3)	Does baby need a fluid bolus? Give 10ml/kg 0.9% Sodium Chloride if signs of shock and no signs of heart failure 
4)	Check blood sugar. Give 2-3ml/kg 10% Dextrose if less than 2.6mmol/L or if baby is symptomatic

diagnoses.name: Weight loss >10% from birth/ inadequate weight gain
diagnoses.text1:
Admit: 
-A baby who has lost more than 10% of birth weight 
-A baby who continues to lose weight
-A baby who has not regained their birth weight by 2 weeks (for prem babies age 10 days term age 7 days) 

Assess for: 
o	Signs of Shock (cold hands and feet, prolonged CRT, lethargic or reduced consciousness)
o	Dehydration (reduced number of wet nappies*, sleepy or weak) - Normal number of wet nappies: at least as many per day as the day of life (eg at least 3 on day 3)
o	Jaundice (measure bilirubin and plot on the chart according to the weight or use the Kramer stages (picture 1)
o	Consider hypernatremia 
o	Feeding and milk supply (See image box around effective and ineffective feeding) 
o	Underlying causes other than poor intake
o	Measure and plot length, weight and head circumference
diagnoses.text2:
Investigations: 
•	Blood Glucose, U&Es
•	Consider Septic screen: Blood culture and lumbar puncture 
•	Consider Bilirubin if jaundiced 

Management
•	Discuss with senior 
•	If signs of shock give 10ml/kg 0.9% Sodium Chloride or Ringers Lactate IV bolus 
•	If blood sugar less than 2.6mmol/L give 10% Dextrose 2ml/kg. If symptoms of hypoglycaemia (eg. jittery, sleepy) OR if unable to measure blood sugar level give regardless
•	Keep warm 
•	Consider underlying cause for weight loss and further investigations and treatment 
•	Assess physical and mental health of the mother

Feeds
•	Continue breastfeeding and encourage skin to skin with mother where possible 
•	Feed 2-3 hourly for around 15-20 minutes then offer top up feed 
•	If baby is not able to take the full feeds need to insert OGD or NG tube for feeding   
•	If mother has limited milk supply there Formula top up may be prescribed, while milk supply is improving
•	Reweigh after 24 hours

Supplementation if low birth weight (from 2 weeks to 6 months of age)
•	Vitamin D 800 IU once daily 
•	Iron 3-6mg/kg once daily

diagnoses.name: Jaundice
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: Every baby with Jaundice above the treatment line needs phototherapy. Always treat if jaundice of palms and soles: if bilirubin not immediately available refer to the Kramer stages
diagnoses.text1:
Assessment: 
Stabilise baby  (A,B,C,D)
Full examination to look for signs of dehydration, pallor, infection 
Plot weight, length and head circumference
Check the colour of stools and urines
Assess jaundice using the Kramer scale
 
Investigations:
- Transcutaneous bilirubin or serum Bilirubin 
- If requiring phototherapy : FBC, Split Bilirubin (conjugated and unconjugated) liver function tests, consider syphilis serology 
- If jaundice on day 1 or concern about haemolytic disease of the newborn: blood type of infant and mother and Coombs test 
- If prolonged jaundice: consider thyroid function tests,
- If surgical causes suspected (= pale/white stools and dark urine)  liver ultra sound scan
diagnoses.text2:
Management:
•	Start phototherapy if 
o	Bilirubin is over the phototherapy
•	If not able to measure Bilirubin start phototherapy if there is: 
o	jaundice of hands and feet (see Kramer stages) 
o	Jaundice on day 1
o	Jaundice due to haemolysis
o	Prematurity and jaundice
•	Encourage breastfeeding a minimum of every 3 hours. Babies on phototherapy can need up to an extra 20ml/kg/24 hours of fluid. Monitor input and urine output
•	If concerns about milk supply encourage top ups after each feed at 150ml/kg/24 hours
•	If weight loss also present – will need feeding support – see weight loss guideline
•	If fever or hypothermia (not environmental) are present – consider neonatal sepsis
•	When under phototherapy keep baby exposed except for nappy and cover the eyes of the baby Keep baby warm! 
•	Continue phototherapy until serum Bilirubin is at least 50 lower than the threshold range. 
•	Re-check Bilirubin 12-24 hours after stopping phototherapy.

diagnoses.name: Diarrhoea and dehydration
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: DEHYDRATION SECONDARY TO DIARRHOEA AND VOMITING ONLY
diagnoses.text1: For the management of a baby who has lost weight, has faltering growth or jaundice see specific guidelines. If a baby has diarrhoea/vomiting ask specifically about blood in the stool, fever, type and frequency of stools and vomit.
diagnoses.text3:
Advise mother of danger signs if discharged: 
-Unable to breastfeed
-Fever / hypothermia
-Blood in the stool 
-Not improving after 5 days

Signs of dehydration in a neonate are harder to assess. Consider also reduced urine output/wet nappies, weight loss and jaundice. 

Blood tests: FBC, U&Es, CRP, Stool MC&S, BC and Urine cultures, if BC positive consider LP

In all cases give Zinc 10mg (half tablet) once per day for 10-14 days. Dissolve the tablet in a small amount of clean water, expressed breast milk or ORS in a small cup or spoon.

diagnoses.name: HIV Exposed
diagnoses.expressionMeaning: All HIV exposed infants should receive prophylaxis with triple therapy.
diagnoses.text1: MANAGEMENT
diagnoses.text2: FOR INFANTS UNDER 12 WEEKS OF AGE AND UNDER 2000G
diagnoses.text3:
TESTING AND OTHER

Infants should have a DNA PCR/NAT as soon as possible after delivery 
Results need to be chased as treatment needs to change if the baby tests positive

Prescribe Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis from 6 weeks of age until final confirmation of a negative HIV status (defined as a negative 18-month test or testing after breastfeeding ends if breastfed longer than 18 months)

diagnoses.text2: 2. Increase frequency of feeds e.g. from 3 to 2 hourly or from 2 to 1 hourly

- If 3 normal blood sugars (2.6 - 8.3mmol), monitoring can be stopped

Includes:
Neural tube defect 
Cleft palate 

1. Refer to surgeons
Specifically refer to orthopaedics for bone injuries or abnormalities
diagnoses.text2:
2. Treat for sepsis / risk of sepsis 

If there is any fever 38.0 or more treat with antibiotics 
Neural tube defects are high risk for sepsis and meningitis

diagnoses.name: Dehydration
diagnoses.expression: $HPCS = 'PF' or $HPCS = 'NG' or $HPCS = 'Wtloss' or $Feed_Amount = 'RedInt' or $Feed_Amount = 'NotFeed' or $Nappy_n = 0 or $Fontanelle = 'Sunk' or $HydStat = 'SE' or $HydStat = 'PSP' or $HydStat = 'DMM'
diagnoses.text1:
Refer to WHO plan A, B or C as below:

Plan A

Give extra fluid orally:
Breastfeed frequently and for longer each feed
If infant vomits, wait 10 minutes then start again
If continues to vomit, will need clinic review
diagnoses.text2:
Plan B

Give 75ml/kg over 4 hours orally
Either by frequent breast feeds or cup feeds with EBM/formula
Reassess dehydration after 4 hours and select appropriate plan (A, B, C) to continue. 
If vomits, wait for 10 minutes then continue to offer feeds but more slowly
diagnoses.text3:
Plan C: Severe Dehydration


Give iv fluids10% dextrose or Ringers Lactate. 
Give first 30ml/kg in 1 hour, then 70ml/kg in 5 hours. 
Continue to offer breast/ cup feeds as tolerated

Reassess every 1-2 hours. If not improving, increase drip rate and check renal function
Monitor urine output
At 6 hours, reassess dehydration status and continue with plan A, B or C as appropriate

managementMetadata.title: Consider Congenital Heart Disease
managementMetadata.title2: 2. Duct Dependent for systemic blood flow
managementMetadata.text1:
Cyanosis/bradycardia at birth should be assumed to be RESPIRATORY not cardiac

Cardiac lesions causing poor conditions at birth are rare (e.g. Ebstein's anomaly or arrhythmia with hydrops)

Cardiac lesions can present when babies are hours/days old. 

1. Keep warm, monitor and feed

Monitor oxygen saturations. 

Consider treating for sepsis if requiring significant support

Use naso/orogastric feeds to decrease work of breathing

Organise an Echo and CXR

Monitor for signs of heart failure and consider diuretics
managementMetadata.text2:
If left sided obstructive duct dependent heart disease suspected (e.g. hypoplastic left heart or aortic stenosis) 
- Insert a UVC
- Commence prostaglandin infusion at 10 nanograms/kg/min or PO 0.01-0.02 mg/kg/dose by NGT

- Aim for O2 saturations of >75%. Reduce inspired O2 if sats >85%
managementMetadata.text3:
These include pulmonary atresia and critical pulmonary stenosis

Aim for sats >75%
- commence a prostaglandin as above
- if develops apnoeas or if sats <75% despite prostaglandin, ventilation should be initiated.
- if apnoeas but sats >75%, reduce prostaglandin, but not below 5 ng/kg/min.

managementMetadata.title: Pneumonia / Bronchiolitis
managementMetadata.text1:
Position airway & suction
If sats < 90% in air put on oxygen
If > 1 kg consider CPAP according to TRY algorithm
managementMetadata.text2:
If breathing 60-80 bpm use cup/NGT
If needing CPAP use OGT
If breathing > 80bpm consider IV fluids
managementMetadata.text3:
Investigations: FBC including differential

Blood cultures- take BEFORE commencing antibiotics if possible
Remember to write the Neotree number on the bottle and form (first 3 and last 3 digits of full number)

Lumbar puncture if signs of meningism
CRP if available. 

Commence: X pen 50000 iu/kg/dose 12 hourly
gentamicin 5 mg/kg/dose 24 hourly 

Reduce gentamicin to 4 mg/kg/dose if <2000g

Stop at 48 hours if Cultures/investigations negative AND symptoms resolved.

managementMetadata.contentText:
Baby's gestation is 32 weeks to 36 weeks

Most stable larger preterm babies (>1500g) not needing oxygen may safely be nursed with their mother in Kangaroo Care. 
Remember to perform Ballard Score- images are for neuromuscular followed by physical maturity assessment  - (Ballard score images in script)


WARM CHAIN is maintained: 
•	Keep the radiant warmer or resucitaire on
•	For babies < 32 weeks deliver into plastic bag before drying if available. If not, dry infant in warm 
towel and wrap in another dry warm towel.
•	Put skin to skin with mother and cover both with blanket
•	Keep room/transport incubator/ambulance (if transporting) as warm as possible.
•	Ensure baby has a hat & socks, and perform procedures in the incubator.
managementMetadata.title: Premature (32-36 weeks)
managementMetadata.text1:
Keep the baby warm aiming between 36.5-37.5’C by Skin to skin (KMC position) or place on radiant warmer or incubator if available

Mild hypothermia: 36-36.4 --> cause for concern,  warm the baby

Moderate hypothermia: 32-35.9--> DANGER
•	rewarm baby,  
•	check blood glucose

Severe hypothermia <32, outcome likely to be poor, 
•	rewarm baby, 
•	check blood glucose
managementMetadata.text2:
•	Oxygen / CPAP
•	CPAP >28 weeks or > 1000g and passes the TRY CPAP algorithm (image in script)
•	Remember preterms may have slightly reduced tone due to their prematurity
•	Early CPAP for babies between 28 - 32 weeks
•	Prevention of apnoea Give Caffeine Citrate 20mg/kg orally or slowly by intravenous route over 30 minutes and a maintenance dose of 5mg/kg/day to all preterm babies<32 weeks. Give until 34 weeks postnestrual age.
•	If Caffeine citrate is not available give a loading dose of aminophylline at 6mg/kg over 20 minutes followed by a maintenance dose of 2.5mg/kg every 12 hours
managementMetadata.text3:
•	If able to suck GIVE breast feed
•	If not able to suck give cup feeds or consider OGT 
•	OGT for all babies < 1500g, RR > 60 and needing respiratory support
•	OGT if on CPAP
•	Consider IV fluids in smaller babies breathing > 80 bpm

managementMetadata.contentText: Prolonged jaundice > 14 days term or >21 days preterm infants
managementMetadata.title: Prolonged Jaundice
managementMetadata.text1:
Liver/metabolic disorder – Perform liver function tests and calculate percentage of conjugated to 
unconjugated bilirubin (if more than 20% it is conjugated hyperbilirubinemia)
Hypothyroidism  - perform thyroid function tests if available
Biliary atresia  - perform abdominal USS if conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and pale stools

Take the TSB as well if possible.

managementMetadata.title: Hypoxic Ischaemic Encephalopathy (HIE)
managementMetadata.text1:
ABCD (Airway, Breathing, Circulation, "Don't forget Glucose")
Prevent hyperthermia
Start feeds to maximum of 40ml/kg/day
Observe for 72 hours
managementMetadata.text2:
Check glucose  if  < 45 mg/dl or < 2.5 mmol/L give IV 10% glucose at 2ml/kg
Load with phenobarbitone (20mg/kg IM)
Check U&Es,Ca,Mg,PO4
If ongoing seizures, repeat loading dose of phenobarbitone and start maintenance (5mg/kg oral or IM)
Monitor respirations
managementMetadata.text3:
Start antibiotics. Covering for meningitis
If baby has normal neurological examination after 72 hours and has been seizure free for 48 hours ,stop phenobarbitone.

If baby has abnormal neurology/ convulsions at 72 hours to discuss with senior paediatrican

managementMetadata.text1:
Primary repair is considered on day 1 if infant is less than 6 hours old and all bowel is viable.
If there are signs of sepsis or non-viable bowel (conduct PEEL Score) then surgeons apply a silo bag
If it’s viable and <6 hrs the surgeons do primary repair on day 1. If there are signs of sepsis or distended bowels, then you add a silo bag.
managementMetadata.text3:
If possible, conduct a blood culture and then start triple antibiotics
Ampicillin (25-50mg/kg IV four times a day) and
Amikacin (7.5mg/kg IV once a day) and
Metronidazole (15mg/kg as a single loading dose, followed by 7.5mg/kg every 12hr starting 24 hr after the loading dose)


Counsel and educate parents
Encourage parental bonding

managementMetadata.contentText: Baby has a small sac protruding from the back or the head
managementMetadata.title: Myelomeningocele
managementMetadata.title1: 1. Handle with sterile, latex-free gloves (if possible) and sterile towels at delivery
managementMetadata.text1:
Nurse side-lying or prone to ensure no pressure is placed on the lesion
Wrap lesion with sterile gauze soaked in warm saline
managementMetadata.text2:
Apply topical tetracycline and give IV Benzylpenicillin (100-150 mg/kg daily in two divided doses) or Ampicillin (25-50 mg/kg IM or IV four times a day) PLUS Amikacin for 5 days

Refer to Paediatric Neurosurgeon for closure.
managementMetadata.text3:
Monitor daily head circumference  and obtain Cranial USS and CT (if CrUSS is of concern and possible) 
Monitor for symptoms of bowel, bladder and motor deficit and hydrocephalus (apnoea, bradycardia, hypoventilation, stridor, swallow dysfunction)

managementMetadata.actionText: Every baby with Jaundice above the treatment line needs phototherapy. Always treat if jaundice of palms and soles: if bilirubin not immediately available refer to the Kramer stages
managementMetadata.title: Jaundice
managementMetadata.text1:
Assessment: 
Stabilise baby  (A,B,C,D)
Full examination to look for signs of dehydration, pallor, infection 
Plot weight, length and head circumference
Check the colour of stools and urines
Assess jaundice using the Kramer scale
 
Investigations:
- Transcutaneous bilirubin or serum Bilirubin 
- If requiring phototherapy : FBC, Split Bilirubin (conjugated and unconjugated) liver function tests, consider syphilis serology 
- If jaundice on day 1 or concern about haemolytic disease of the newborn: blood type of infant and mother and Coombs test 
- If prolonged jaundice: consider thyroid function tests,
- If surgical causes suspected (= pale/white stools and dark urine)  liver ultra sound scan
managementMetadata.text2:
Management:
•	Start phototherapy if 
o	Bilirubin is over the phototherapy
•	If not able to measure Bilirubin start phototherapy if there is: 
o	jaundice of hands and feet (see Kramer stages) 
o	Jaundice on day 1
o	Jaundice due to haemolysis
o	Prematurity and jaundice
•	Encourage breastfeeding a minimum of every 3 hours. Babies on phototherapy can need up to an extra 20ml/kg/24 hours of fluid. Monitor input and urine output
•	If concerns about milk supply encourage top ups after each feed at 150ml/kg/24 hours
•	If weight loss also present – will need feeding support – see weight loss guideline
•	If fever or hypothermia (not environmental) are present – consider neonatal sepsis
•	When under phototherapy keep baby exposed except for nappy and cover the eyes of the baby Keep baby warm! 
•	Continue phototherapy until serum Bilirubin is at least 50 lower than the threshold range. 
•	Re-check Bilirubin 12-24 hours after stopping phototherapy.

managementMetadata.title: Neonatal sepsis
managementMetadata.text1: Consider neonatal severe infections if any Major Criteria or two or more Minor Criteria are met:
managementMetadata.text3:
MANAGEMENT
Keep baby warm and aim for temperature between 36.5-37.5 
Stabilise the infant using the ABCD resuscitation principles 

TAKE:
1)	Blood culture 
(REMEMBER to put the Neotree number on the blood culture bottle, minimise contamination by cleaning well with disinfectant and leave the area to dry, put AT LEAST 1-2 ml in the blood culture bottle) DON’T delay giving antibiotics if blood culture not possible 
2)	Perform a Lumbar puncture in ALL babies under 2 months of age 
3)	Urine Dipstick and culture for LOS: urine culture need to be sterile, need to clean the perineum. Don’t delay antibiotics to wait for urine culture – do not send if you cannot catch a sterile sample
GIVE: 
1)	Antibiotics (see below)
2)	Oxygen if sats <90% in air
3)	Does baby need a fluid bolus? Give 10ml/kg 0.9% Sodium Chloride if signs of shock and no signs of heart failure 
4)	Check blood sugar. Give 2-3ml/kg 10% Dextrose if less than 2.6mmol/L or if baby is symptomatic

managementMetadata.actionText: The best approach to feed a baby depends on their birth weight, gestation, ability to suck effectively and how well the baby is.
managementMetadata.title: Feed and Fluid Guideline
managementMetadata.title3: Type of fluids and breastmilk fortification
managementMetadata.text1:
Healthy babies more than 34 weeks are usually able to suck unless they are ill
•	Breastfeed and encourage exclusive breastfeeding
•	Initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of life

For sick and or premature infant who is unable to suck
•	Give expressed breast milk (EBM) via Nasogastric or orogastric tube or cup
•	Use formula feeds only if EBM is not available
•	Preterm Infant milk formula if < 2000g and <35 weeks
•	Standard infant formula ≥ 2000g

• Infants ≥ 1500g and ≥ 32 weeks can be started on feeds at 60mls/kg/day and increase by 30mls/kg/day as tolerated to a maximum of 150mls/kg/day for term babies and 200mls/kg/day for preterm infants

• Infants < 1500g or < 32 weeks should receive IV fluids to allow gradual increase of enteral feeds. These infants are kept nil by mouth immediately after birth (unless mother’s colostrum is present) Consider colostrum/EBM for mouth cares in those <1500g in first 24 hours. Discuss with senior if unsure.
managementMetadata.text2:
The table below demonstrates feed volumes 

-Always use the HIGHEST weight to calculate feeds or fluid volumes (this may be birth weight or current weight) 

-Usually feeds are started 3 hourly but 2 hourly feeds may be useful in very small babies or those not tolerating 3 hourly feeds 

-If the drip tissues and patient is tolerating at least 140ml/kg/day orally then no need to continue IV fluids
managementMetadata.text3:
-5% or 10% Dextrose in the first 36-48 hours of life
-Electrolytes to be added to fluids after this point
-Blood glucose must be monitored in the first 36-48 hours and then can be stopped if normal.
